data.title: Middle East Eye: Three years after Israeli bombing, Palestinian man recovers wife's remains
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
Three years after Israeli bombing, Palestinian man recovers wife's remains
For nearly three years, Adham Heriz, 41, waited to recover and bury the bodies of his wife and children.
On Thursday, after years of searching through the ruins of their neighbourhood in eastern Gaza City, the Palestinian father finally recovered the remains of his wife, Hiam, 37. His son’s body is still missing.
Hiam and their eldest son, Anas, 17, were killed when a heavy Israeli bombardment completely destroyed their home in Al-Yarmouk on 25 October 2023.
According to the Palestinian civil defence spokesperson in Gaza, Mahmoud Basal, the attack involved a series of heavy Israeli bombardments that struck 18 buildings containing around 175 residential apartments.
Around 450 people were inside the buildings, including doctors, academics, journalists, children and infants, Basal told MEE.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Turkey supplies Korkut air defence systems to Ukraine, sources say
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Turkey supplies Korkut air defence systems to Ukraine, sources say
Turkey supplied anti-drone air defence systems to Ukraine earlier this year, allowing Kyiv to test new products and bolster its capabilities, several people familiar with the matter told Middle East Eye.
The sources said Ukraine had imported a small number of Turkish-made Korkut air defence systems, which typically consist of three weapon system vehicles and one command-and-control vehicle. They declined to disclose how many units had been deployed on the battlefield.
Produced by Aselsan, Korkut uses air defence guns to shoot down aerial targets, including the cruise missiles and drones that have become a persistent threat in the war in Ukraine. The system is designed to counter first-person-view and tethered drones using 25-millimetre smart ammunition.
“Korkut has been pretty much successful in countering the Russian attacks,” one Ukrainian official told MEE, speaking on condition of anonymity due to government restrictions. “There were of course some problems but nothing that couldn’t be overcome through some small adjustments.”
The official said Korkut could be considered battle-proven and that Ukraine was interested in purchasing more systems.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Labour MP Emily Thornberry urges UK to defy Israeli order to close Jerusalem consulate
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Labour MP Emily Thornberry urges UK to defy Israeli order to close Jerusalem consulate
Emily Thornberry, chair of parliament’s influential Foreign Affairs Committee, has called on Britain to refuse compliance with Israel’s closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem.
Her intervention comes amidst mounting anxiety among Palestinians that Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband will submit to Israeli pressure and shut the consulate on Thursday.
Middle East Eye understands that the foreign secretary’s decision is being watched closely by other consulates, including France and Spain, who fear they will be next to be forced out if the British quit.
Thornberry told MEE on Monday that the closure of the consulate was a “blatant retaliation against Britain for standing up for international law. The closure order is in itself illegal.”
“I hope that Israel will not go through with the closure of a consulate which has served Britons and Palestinians since 1838. Britain should not allow Israel to do this,” she said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Father of man killed by Israeli fire during 7 October calls Netanyahu a traitor
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Father of man killed by Israeli fire during 7 October calls Netanyahu a traitor
The father of an Israeli man killed by Israeli military fire during the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023 has branded Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "traitor", and told him: "You did not protect my son."
According to Israeli outlet Ynet, Yaakov Godo, the father of Tom Godo, interrupted Netanyahu as the Israeli prime minister delivered a speech marking the third anniversary of the attack at Mount Herzl in Jerusalem on Monday.
“It’s a disgrace that you didn’t protect those murdered on October 7,” Yaakov Godo shouted out. “The blood of my son and of another 1,200 people murdered in a single day is on his (Netanyahu's) hands and on his head.”
Tom Godo was killed by Israeli military gunfire after the Hannibal Directive was invoked while sheltering in his home at Kibbutz Kissufim with his wife and three daughters.
Netanyahu briefly interrupted Yaakov's speech. "I wanted to tell him he was a traitor - but I couldn't," Godo said afterwards.
“I managed to stand up to him once. I don't have many opportunities to meet him. It was important to me to tell him that the blood of my son and the blood of 1,200 other people murdered in one day - it's on his hands and on his head," the bereaved father continued.
"He never turned to talk to us. No one came to us and no one even informed us that Tom was killed. Only the army came after a year and a half and said that it was sorry and that Tom was shot by army soldiers,” Godo said.

data.author: Alex MacDonald
data.summary:
Thousands transferred from Syria to Iraq face possible execution over alleged IS links, HRW says
Submitted by
Alex MacDonald
on

Dozens of countries have stalled repatriating their nationals as Baghdad prepares to prosecute alleged Islamic State members under its counterterrorism law
An Iraqi police patrol transports Iraqi detainees into the grounds of the Karkh Courthouse in Baghdad on 5 October 2026 (Ahmad al-Rubaye/AFP)
Off
Thousands of men and boys suspected of links to the Islamic State (IS) group are at risk of abuse and unfair prosecution in Iraq, Human Rights Watch (HRW) has warned.
According to the group, nearly 5,700 men and boys from a range of countries are at risk of abuse, including imminent prosecution of adults in unfair trials, followed by the death penalty.
There have also been reports of widespread torture, unsanitary conditions and deaths in custody.
The detainees - about 3,500 from Syria and 2,200 from Iraq and dozens of other countries - had already been held in life-threatening conditions for up to seven-and-a-half years in northeast Syria before being transferred to Iraq between 21 January and 12 February this year.
Letta Tayler, senior counterterrorism advisor at HRW, said in a statement: “The thousands of boys and men sent to Iraq deserve humane treatment and due process, just as the thousands of survivors of ISIS crimes deserve genuine justice.
“The international community shouldn’t leave Iraq to manage this immense responsibility on its own.”
HRW said that foreign countries needed to take responsibility for their citizens and repatriate them.
Fair trial concerns
IS swept across Syria and Iraq in 2014, capturing large swathes of both countries.
Backed by US-led forces, Iraq declared victory over IS's territorial presence in 2017, while the group lost its last territorial stronghold in Syria in 2019.
As the US pulls its forces out of Iraq, what happens to Iran-backed armed groups?

data.author: Peter Oborne

Channel 4 investigation shows how the UK government repeatedly failed to hold the Israeli army to account for war crimes
Pro-Palestinian activists and supporters gather in central London to protest British arms exports to Israel, on 17 April 2024 (Justin Tallis/AFP)
Off
Twenty-five years have passed since sociologist Stanley Cohen asked a question that remains just as urgent today as it was when he first posed it.
How is it that institutions, governments and ordinary people can know about atrocities, mass killing and human rights abuses, but simultaneously manage to put them out of their minds?
His brilliant study, States of Denial: Knowing About Atrocities and Suffering , drew on Cohen’s own reporting of cover-ups, disappearances and torture in his native South Africa. Yet its examination of the ways in which we pretend to ourselves that terrible events are not taking place was broader, taking in Latin America, the Rwanda genocide, the Holocaust, the Middle East and other examples.
Cohen distinguished between the different ways in which politicians, journalists and others have suppressed knowledge of the truth. He identified what he called “literal denial” - the unblinking assertion that crimes are not taking place.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s recent speech to the United Nations contained numerous examples of literal denial. He said that the ratio of civilian casualties to combatants in Gaza was exceptionally low, that Israel did not block aid to Gaza, and that Hamas should be blamed for shortages.
He also made the nonsensical assertion that settler violence in the occupied West Bank was down to a “handful of young juvenile delinquents”.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the deployment of weapons into outer space, following recent disclosures that armed military assets have already been placed in Earth’s orbit.
Speaking at a high-profile space conference attended by diplomats and space agency representatives, Erdogan called for the cosmos to remain peaceful for scientific exploration rather than the next arena of military conflict.
"Sending weapons to space, or turning space into a ground for an arms race, will be totally wrong," Erdogan told the International Astronautical Conference (IAC) in Antalya, southern Turkey on Monday.
"It will be a direct threat to the joint future for humanity, and I see that this race is becoming widespread - which, of course, we do not welcome."
Erdogan is the first Nato leader to issue a condemnation of space weapons after the United States last month publicly acknowledged for the first time that it had deployed a space weapon into Earth’s orbit.
Israel had also hinted at plans to develop space weapons to defend Israeli satellites from hostile spacecraft and weapons capable of striking Earth from outerspace.
US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink confirmed that the “on-orbit” weapon had been placed in Earth’s orbit to counter “evolving threats,” but did not say when it was put into orbit.

An Israeli mathematics lecturer has been indicted over an alleged plan to kill hundreds of Palestinian citizens of Israel and Palestinians in the occupied territories, and force them from their homes.
Israeli news outlet Yedioth Ahronoth reported that the man, a professor at Bar-Ilan University in his 60s, was accused of developing a detailed plan for simultaneous attacks on Palestinian communities, Bedouin communities, and mixed cities, according to an indictment filed by prosecutors.
His name is under a court-imposed gag order.
Prosecutors allege that he planned to recruit 72 Jewish attackers, including himself, and divide them into 12 cells of six people.
The groups would have been armed with firearms, axes and hammers and would have launched coordinated attacks designed to cause mass casualties and spread fear, according to the indictment.
The alleged targets included Palestinian citizens of Israel, Bedouin communities, Palestinians in occupied East Jerusalem and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Prosecutors say the objective was to cause Palestinians to flee or be permanently expelled towards Jordan, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip.
The lecturer allegedly called his plan "AIT," an acronym for the Hebrew phrase "the nation will carry out transfer".
According to the indictment, he began developing the plan in February 2023, following communal violence in Israel in 2021, and intensified his efforts after the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.

Iran's president says negotiations with US are meaningless, state media reports
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said negotiations with the US are meaningless, according to state media.
There is no point in negotiating with "an enemy that terrorizes, sanctions, pressures, and threatens on a daily basis", he said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump says rise of petrol prices no longer due to Strait of Hormuz
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
Trump says rise of petrol prices no longer due to Strait of Hormuz
In a post on Truth Social, US President Donald Trump stated that the rise in petrol prices is no longer due to the Strait of Hormuz.
Instead, Trump said that the blowing up of Russian refineries and the closing of US refineries in some states are the actual reasons behind the spike in petrol prices.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Makkah alliance to activate 'collective deterrence', Saudi Arabia's minister of defence announces
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
Makkah alliance to activate 'collective deterrence', Saudi Arabia's minister of defence announces
Saudi Minister of Defence Prince Khaled bin Salman announced that the Makkah alliance will activate "collective deterrence" amid the current escalation with the Houthis in Yemen, following an emergency meeting of the alliance's Strategic Political and Defence Committee in Riyadh.
The meeting "reaffirmed the solidarity and unity of our countries in confronting the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and the holy sites", the statement added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemen: Video shows armoured vehicle ramming unarmed and armed men as fighting rages
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Yemen: Video shows armoured vehicle ramming unarmed and armed men as fighting rages
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Mon, 10/05/2026 - 17:46
The vehicle mows down men who clearly have their hands raised to surrender, in addition to men armed with rifles
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces ride in the back of a military truck at the Jabal Han front, west of the city of Taiz, following fierce battles earlier in the day, on 3 October 2026 (Ahmad al-Basha/AFP)
Off
Multiple videos have emerged on social media showing what appear to be Yemeni-government-aligned soldiers in an armoured vehicle driving over bodies and armed and unarmed men amid a counter-offensive against the Houthis.
One video shows the driver of the armoured vehicle moving into a crowd of men, some armed with rifles but others clearly holding up their hands to surrender.
The driver clearly mows the vehicle into two men who have their arms raised to surrender. The driver and his companion then scream “Allahu Akbar” as they drive over several prone men on the side of the road; some lie motionless, and others twitch their legs. The camera's movements capture the thumps of the vehicle hitting the bodies.
At the beginning of the video, one can hear the click-clack of small arms fire, although it is not clear who is shooting.
A second video appears to show a man on the ground pointing an assault rifle at the vehicle as it comes towards him. Small arms fire can be heard in the background. After hitting the first man, the driver takes the vehicle into a crowd of men who are lying on the ground. The men raise their weapons and begin to shoot at the vehicle as it accelerates towards them.
A third video appears to show the vehicle searching for men to ram after engaging the last group. The driver finds an armed man lying alone on the beach. data.title: Middle East Eye: US mission issues warning for US citizens in Saudi Arabia
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
US mission issues warning for US citizens in Saudi Arabia
The US mission in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert for American citizens in the kingdom amid the ongoing escalations with the Houthis in Yemen.
"Due to the ongoing security situation in Saudi Arabia and the potential for aerial drone or missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, the US Mission strongly encourages all US citizens to remain vigilant and follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense," the alert said.
